# Portrait lenses — lightweight Canon RF

**Dimension:** lightweight Canon-brand RF/RF-S lenses for portraits. Source
detail in [citations.md](../citations.md); terms in [glossary](../glossary.md).

## Why ~50–85 mm + a low f-number flatters faces

Longer focal lengths compress perspective so features look natural (wide lenses
up close distort faces), and a wide aperture (low f-number) blurs the background
to separate the subject [[27]](../citations.md#c27). On **APS-C** add the 1.6×
crop: a 50 mm acts like ~80 mm, an 85 mm like ~136 mm
[[28]](../citations.md#c28).

## Recommendation logic

- **Lightest + cheapest:** RF 50mm f/1.8 STM (160 g). On APS-C its ~80 mm view
  is ideal for portraits [[20]](../citations.md#c20)[[28]](../citations.md#c28).
- **Best dual-purpose:** RF 85mm f/2 Macro IS STM — flattering portrait reach,
  has IS, and doubles as a 0.5× macro lens for the later macro goal
  [[22]](../citations.md#c22). Note: ~136 mm-equiv on APS-C is long for indoor
  family headshots in small rooms.
- **On APS-C for indoor family:** the RF 35mm f/1.8 (~56 mm-equiv) is more
  practical indoors and adds close-focus [[23]](../citations.md#c23).

## Counter-perspectives

- **You may not need a portrait prime:** a quality 24–105 zoom at 105 mm makes
  good portraits; for a beginner, zoom flexibility can beat marginal extra blur
  [[27]](../citations.md#c27) (see [versatile-lenses](versatile-lenses.md)).
- **f/1.8 vs f/1.2 is oversold:** the look difference is incremental and rarely
  worth the f/1.2L's weight/price for a beginner [[27]](../citations.md#c27).
- **No Canon-brand RF-S portrait prime exists** — APS-C buyers use full-frame RF
  primes (focal math shifts) or third-party Sigma primes
  [[29]](../citations.md#c29) (see [third-party-lenses](third-party-lenses.md)).

## Gaps and limitations

- Lens weights are review-site/manufacturer figures via search snippets
  (The Digital Picture, Dustin Abbott) — Canon spec pages were fetch-blocked.
  RF 35mm and RF 85mm f/2 weights are corroborated by PhotoWorkout's directly
  fetched data [[36]](../citations.md#c36).
- RF 50mm f/1.8 price band ($199–249) varies by promotion.
